explanation: Modern computer systems employ a memory hierarchy to bridge the performance gap between fast but expensive CPU and slow but cheap storage.  This hierarchy consists of multiple levels of memory with varying speed and capacity.  Faster, smaller caches (SRAM) are placed closer to the CPU, while slower, larger main memory (DRAM) and slower still, massive secondary storage (disks or SSDs) are further away.  The principle of locality of reference—that recently accessed data is likely to be accessed again soon—is exploited to make this system efficient. Data is copied up the hierarchy as needed, providing fast access to frequently used data while maintaining the overall cost-effectiveness of the larger, slower storage.
syntax: No specific syntax, but the concept is implemented through hardware and operating system mechanisms that manage data movement between different memory levels (caches, main memory, secondary storage) based on access patterns and replacement policies (e.g., LRU, FIFO).
code_example: ; Example illustrating cache behavior (conceptual, not real assembly)
; Assume a simple CPU with a small cache and main memory
; Data is initially in main memory
mov eax, [memory_address] ; Access data from main memory (cache miss)
; Data is now loaded into the cache
mov ebx, [memory_address] ; Access data from cache (cache hit)
mov ecx, [another_memory_address]; Access different data (cache miss)
mov edx, [memory_address]; Access original data again (cache hit)
example_explanation: The example demonstrates the concept of cache hits and misses.  The first access (`mov eax, [memory_address]`) results in a cache miss because the data is not in the cache.  The data is then loaded from main memory into the cache. Subsequent accesses to the same data (`mov ebx, [memory_address]`) will be cache hits since the data is now present in the faster cache.  Accessing different data results in another cache miss, highlighting that the cache is limited in size and only holds a portion of the main memory data.  The final access shows another cache hit due to data already present in the cache illustrating the efficiency gained from locality.
